sentences.text: Epachthosaurus was a large titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur whose name translates to "heavy lizard".

This animal reached lengths of approximately 18 to 20 meters and likely lacked the bony armor seen in relatives like Saltasaurus. It is considered the most basal titanosaurid possessing procoelous caudal vertebrae, which have a concave front surface.
The skeleton is distinguished by unique features, including hyposphene-hypantrum articulations in the first fourteen caudal vertebrae and a specific pedal phalangeal formula of 2-2-3-2-0.
A 2004 study estimated the weight of specimen UNPSJB-PV 920 at 11,290 kilograms using a water displacement method.
Despite its significance, there are only three recorded fossil occurrences of this genus known to science.
The genus Epachthosaurus was named by Powell in 1990, with the type species designated as Epachthosaurus sciuttoi.
The holotype specimen, MACN-CH 1317, consists of an incomplete posterior dorsal vertebra.

A nearly complete specimen, UNPSJB-PV 920, was recovered by researchers from the Universidad Nacional de la Patagonia in Argentina. Fossils of Epachthosaurus come from the Bajo Barreal Formation in central Patagonia, Chubut Province, Argentina.
Epachthosaurus shared its environment with basal Chelidae turtles like Bonapartemys and Prochelidella, the abelisaurid Xenotarsosaurus, and an unidentified carnotaurine.
Contemporaries of Epachthosaurus included the sauropod Sarmientosaurus, the ornithopod Notohypsilophodon, and the theropods Drusilasaura, Campylodoniscus, and Aniksosaurus.
Epachthosaurus belongs to the Lithostrotia clade and is classified within the Saurischia class.

Research suggests Epachthosaurus was a basal Titanosauria found between Andesaurus and more highly derived genera. Epachthosaurus, Argentinosaurus, and Andesaurus have been included in the family Andesauridae, characterized by containing the most basal titanosaurs. Epachthosaurus is classified within the family Andesauridae.

Epachthosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 99.6 and 93.5 million years ago. The Bajo Barreal Formation dates to the latest Cenomanian and earliest Turonian of the Cretaceous.

The exact systematic position of Epachthosaurus within Titanosauria is unclear. However, research suggests Epachthosaurus was a basal Titanosauria found between Andesaurus and more highly derived genera.
